title: Worst-case cost from output-conditioned costs
statement: For every $d\in\mathbb{N}$, the worst-case expected query cost of the level-$d$ randomized tree is at most the larger of its two output-conditioned costs: the supremum of the input cost over inputs where the recursive NAND function equals $1$, with cost taken to be zero on all other inputs, and the corresponding supremum for inputs where the function equals $-1$.
